Rashi on Yevamot 26b:1:1.hebrew: חמשה נמי - שנים נשואים שתי אחיות, ומתו השנים ונשארו השלשה; דלמא אדמייבם חד, מייתו להו תרי ובטלה מצות יבמין:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:1:1.english: Five as well - [If] two [of them were] married to two sisters, and the two died and the three remained, perhaps while one performs levirate marriage, [the other] two will die, and the mitzvah of levirate marriage will be nullified.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:2:1.english: Before two brothers [who are] yevamin - That is to say, before two brothers of their husbands, who are their yevamin.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:2:2.hebrew: אמצעית - כלומר שלישית, ולאו דוקא נקט:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:2:2.english: The middle [one] - That is to say, the third [one], and he did not state [it] specifically.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:2:3.english: Requires ḥalitza from both of them - As [it] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:3:1.hebrew: לא גרסינן מדקאמרת זה חולץ כו', אלא ה"ג: מדקאמרת צריכה חליצה משניהם קסברת יש זיקה, והויא לה חליצה פסולה, וחליצה פסולה צריכה לחזור כו' - כלומר, מדקאמרת צריכה חליצה משניהם, קסברת אלימא מצות זיקת יבמין למירמי אתרווייהו, והך חליצה על כרחך חליצה פסולה היא — כלומר גרועה, שאם רצה לייבם אינו יכול, דאחות חלוצתו היא; הילכך לאו מעלייתא היא, וצריכה לחזור על כולן, דלא מיפקעא זיקה דתרווייהו בחליצה דחדא, משום דאלימא זיקה ורמיא אתרווייהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:3:1.english: We do not read "from the fact that you say this one performs chalitzah, etc."; rather, this is the reading: "From the fact that you say she requires chalitzah from both of them, you hold that the levirate bond is substantial, and it is an invalid chalitzah, and an invalid chalitzah must go around, etc." - That is to say: since you say she requires chalitzah from both of them, you hold that the obligation of the levirate bond of the yevamin is strong enough to fall upon both of them. And this chalitzah is perforce an invalid chalitzah — that is to say, an inferior [one], for if he wanted to perform yibbum, he could not, because she is the sister of his chalutzah; therefore, it is not a fully valid [chalitzah], and she must go around to all of them, for the levirate bond of both of them is not dissolved by a single chalitzah, because the levirate bond is strong and falls upon both of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:4:1.hebrew: קמייתא - שתים ראשונות נמי ליבעו חליצה משניהם, דחליצתן נמי לאו מעלייתא היא, דאי בעי לייבומי לא מצי, הואיל ויש זיקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:4:1.english: The first ones - [The] first two [women] should also require ḥalitza from both of them, for their ḥalitza is also not valid, since if they wanted to perform levirate marriage, they could not, because there is a levirate bond [zika].

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:5:1.hebrew: בבת אחת - כלומר, אם באו לחלוץ כאחת, שלא הספיקה הראשונה לחלוץ עד שנפלה גם השניה והשלישית, הכי נמי דכולן צריכות לחזור אחר כל האחין:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:5:1.english: Simultaneously - That is to say, if they came to perform chalitzah at once, such that the first [sister] did not have time to perform chalitzah before the second and third also fell [for levirate marriage], so too [is it], that all of them must go around to all the brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:5:2.english: Here, where they fell one after another - The falling [before the brothers] of one was after the chalitzah of the other.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:6:1.hebrew: נפלה לה חדא חלץ לה ראובן - וחליצה כשרה היתה, שאם רצה יכול לייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:6:1.english: One happened [before them, and] Reuven performed chalitzah with her - And it was a valid chalitzah, for if he wanted, he could have performed levirate marriage [with her].

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:6:2.hebrew: נפלה אידך חלץ לה שמעון - וגם זו כשרה, שאם רצה מייבם, ואין כאן אחות זקוקה, שכבר חלצה אחותה קודם נפילת זו. נפלה שלישית — אי בעי לייבומי לא מצי, דאחות חלוצת שניהם היא, ובולא כלום נמי לא נפקא, דאחות חלוצה אינה אלא מדברי סופרים, לקמן בהחולץ (יבמות דף מ:). הלכך, חלץ האי חליצה כל דהו, ולאו מעלייתא היא, שאם חפץ לא ייבם; ומיהו, חליצתו וזיקתו שוות שתיהן לגרוע, ופקעה זיקתו בחליצתו. חלץ האי — מפקע זיקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:6:2.english: Another [sister] happened [before the brothers], [and] Shimon performed chalitzah with her - This [chalitzah] too is valid, for if he wanted, he could have performed levirate marriage [with her], and there is no [prohibition of] "sister of a woman bound by a levirate bond" here, since her sister had already performed chalitzah prior to this one's falling [before the brothers]. [When] a third [sister] fell [before them] — if [either brother] wanted to perform levirate marriage, he could not, because she is the sister of a woman with whom both of them [i.e., each of them] performed chalitzah; and she also cannot be released with nothing [i.e., without chalitzah], because [the prohibition of] the sister of a woman who received chalitzah is only rabbinic, [as stated] later in [the chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 40b). Therefore, this [brother] performs a minimal chalitzah, and it is not a full-fledged [chalitzah], for if he wanted, he could not perform levirate marriage; nevertheless, his chalitzah and his levirate bond are both equally inferior [in strength], so his levirate bond is terminated by his chalitzah. [Thus, when] this one performs chalitzah, he terminates [his] levirate bond.

Rashi on Yevamot 26b:8:1.hebrew: והא אמר רב אין זיקה - בפרק כיצד (לעיל יבמות דף יז:) א"ר הונא אמר רב: שומרת יבם שמתה, מותר באמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26b:8:1.english: But didn't Rav say: There is no levirate bond? - In Chapter Keitzad (above, Yevamot 17b), Rav Huna said in the name of Rav: [Regarding] a widow awaiting levirate marriage who died, [the levir is] permitted [to marry] her mother.

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:1:1.hebrew: למיתה דתרי לא חיישינן - תימה, דבפ"ק דיומא (דף ב.), גבי הא דאמר ר' יהודה: "אף אשה אחרת מתקינין לו, שמא תמות אשתו", ופרכי לה רבנן: "א"כ, אין לדבר סוף!" ומאי קושיא? הא רבנן חיישי הכא למיתה דחד ולא דתרי! ואר"י, דהכי פרכי ליה: כיון דחיישת למיתה דזמן מועט אע"ג דלא שכיחא, תחוש נמי למיתה דתרי אע"ג דלא שכיח, וא"כ אין לדבר סוף! ומשני התם (דף יג.), דלר' יהודה מיתה דחדא שכיחא — פירוש, אפי' לזמן מועט — דתרי לא שכיחא. והא דקאמרי התם רבנן "מיתה לא שכיחא", לאו משום שאין לדבר סוף, דהא דקאמר "אין לדבר סוף" היינו משום דלא שכיח, כדפרישי'; כי מיתה דחד דשכיח, יש לדבר סוף, דתרי ודאי לא שכיחי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:1:1.english: We are not concerned over the death of two - This is astonishing, for in the first chapter of Yoma (2a), regarding that which Rabbi Yehuda said: "We also designate another wife for him, lest his wife die," and the Rabbis challenged him: "If so, there is no end to the matter!" And what is the difficulty? Behold, the Rabbis are concerned here about the death of one, and not of two! And Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is what they are challenging him: Since you are concerned about death within a short period of time even though it is uncommon, you should also be concerned about the death of two even though it is uncommon, and if so, there is no end to the matter! And [the Gemara] answers there (13a) that according to Rabbi Yehuda, the death of one is common — meaning, even within a short period of time — [whereas the death] of two is uncommon. And that which the Rabbis say there, "Death is uncommon," is not because there is no end to the matter; rather, that which it says, "There is no end to the matter," is because it is uncommon, as I have explained — for [when] the death of one is common, there is an end to the matter, since [the deaths] of two are certainly uncommon.

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:3:1.hebrew: מדקאמרת אמצעית צריכה חליצה משניהם קא סברת יש זיקה וחליצה פסולה וכו' - ואית ספרים דגרסי: "מדקאמר 'זה חולץ לאחת וזה חולץ לאחת', קא סברת יש זיקה", ופי' בקונטרס דלא גרסי' ליה. ונראה דלא גריס ליה בקונטרס, משום דלמ"ד אין זיקה נמי זה חולץ לאחת וזה חולץ לאחת, דאי אפשר לייבם אחת משום ביטול מצות יבמין; וליכא למימר נמי דאחד יחלוץ לשתיהן, דלמ"ד אין זיקה נמי אין חליצה פסולה של ראובן, שכבר חלץ לאחת, מפקעת זיקת שמעון החשובה, דהא לקמן קאמר: "בשלמא צרה דרחל לא תפטר, משום דחליצת רחל חליצה פסולה היא" — אלמא אפי' למ"ד אין זיקה אין חליצת רחל פוטרת זיקת צרתה החשובה, דהא אוקי דשמואל אליבא דמ"ד אין זיקה קאמר; וה"ה דה"נ לא תפטר חליצת ראובן השניה מאח השני, דהא אכתי לא מסיק אדעתיה לחלק בין מיפטר נפשה בין מיפטר צרה. ולר"י נראה דשפיר גרסי' ליה, דלפי האמת למ"ד אין זיקה, חליצה גרועה פוטרת החשובה הימנה, דאמרי' בהדיא בפרק ר"ג (לקמן יבמות דף נא. ושם) דלמ"ד אין זיקה חלץ לבעלת הגט נפטרה צרתה, אע"ג דבעלת הגט חליצתה פסולה טפי משל צרה, שהרי חשובה כחלוצה אצלו למיסר בקרובותיה; וע"כ שמואל, דאמר "חלץ לאחיות לא נפטרו צרות, לבעלת הגט לא נפטרה צרה", סבר דיש זיקה. וסוגיא דבסמוך אינה לפי האמת, אלא ה"פ: "בשלמא צרה דרחל לא תפטר" — כלומר, אפי' אם תאמר דלמ"ד אין זיקה נמי חליצה פסולה צריכה לחזור, והשתא ניחא דצרת רחל לא תפטר, מ"מ צרה דלאה תפטר, דחליצה כשרה היא. תדע דאותה סוגיא אינה לפי האמת, דהא פריך בתר הכי: "ואצרה דרחל מי מיפטרא? והתנן כו'" — אלמא בעי למימר דלמ"ד אין זיקה לא מיפטרא רחל בחליצת צרה, אע"ג דלא אסירא צרה אלא מכחה, וכ"ש אם היו שוות; וא"כ איך מדקדק, אפילו לפי גירסת הקונט', דיש זיקה מדקאמר "אמצעית צריכה חליצה משניהם"? אלא על אותה סוגיא אין לסמוך, כדפרישי' דלא קאי הכי; וכי מפרש דשמואל "התחיל ולא התחיל" קאמר, לא יאמר עוד דשמואל אליבא דמ"ד אין זיקה קאמר, כמו שאפרש דלדידיה חלץ לאחיות ולבעלת הגט נפטרו צרות. וגרסינן שפיר: "מדקאמר 'זה חולץ לאחת כו'', קסבר יש זיקה, ומדקאמר 'אמצעית צריכה חליצה משניהם', קא סבר דחליצה פסולה צריכה לחזור", ואע"ג דתרווייהו יכול לדקדק מסיפא, מ"מ מה שיכול לדקדק מרישא מדקדק:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:3:1.english: "From [the fact] that you say the middle one requires ḥalitza from both of them, you hold [that] the levirate bond is substantial [yesh zikah], and [it is] an invalid ḥalitza, etc." - And there are texts that read: "From [the fact] that it says, 'This one performs ḥalitza with one and this one performs ḥalitza with one,' you hold [that] the levirate bond is substantial," and Rashi explained that we do not read this [text]. And it appears that Rashi does not read it because even according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial [ein zikah], "this one performs ḥalitza with one and this one performs ḥalitza with one," since it is impossible to perform levirate marriage with one [of them] because of [the prohibition of] nullifying the mitzvah of levirate brothers; and one also cannot say that one [brother] should perform ḥalitza with both of them, because even according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, an invalid ḥalitza of Reuven — who has already performed ḥalitza with one — does not release Shimon's superior levirate bond, for later [the Gemara] says: "Granted that Rachel's co-wife is not exempted, because Rachel's ḥalitza is an invalid ḥalitza" — thus, even according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, Rachel's ḥalitza does not exempt the superior levirate bond of her co-wife, since [the Gemara] established that Shmuel spoke in accordance with the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial; and the same applies here as well: Reuven's second ḥalitza would not exempt [her] from the second brother, for [the Gemara] has not yet thought to distinguish between exempting herself and exempting a co-wife. But to R"i it appears that we do indeed read it [that text], for in truth, according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, an inferior ḥalitza exempts one superior to it, as we say explicitly in the chapter [entitled] Rabban Gamliel (below, Yevamot 51a, and there [in the parallel]) that according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, if he performed ḥalitza with the recipient of a bill of divorce, her co-wife is exempted, even though the ḥalitza of the recipient of a bill of divorce is more invalid than that of the co-wife, since she is considered like a ḥalutza to him to forbid [him] in [marrying] her relatives; and perforce, Shmuel — who said, "If he performed ḥalitza with sisters, the co-wives are not exempted; [if] with the recipient of a bill of divorce, the co-wife is not exempted" — holds that the levirate bond is substantial. And the sugya shortly below is not according to the truth [of the law], but rather this is its meaning: "Granted that Rachel's co-wife is not exempted" — meaning, even if you say that even according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, an invalid ḥalitza must be repeated, and now it is understandable that Rachel's co-wife is not exempted, nevertheless Leah's co-wife should be exempted, since it is a valid ḥalitza. Know that that sugya is not according to the truth, for it asks right after that: "And through Rachel's co-wife, is she [Rachel] exempted? Did we not learn [in the Mishnah], etc." — thus it wants to say that according to the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, Rachel is not exempted through the ḥalitza of [her] co-wife, even though the co-wife is only forbidden because of her, and all the more so if they were equal; and if so, how can [the Gemara] infer, even according to Rashi's reading, that the levirate bond is substantial from [the fact] that it says, "The middle one requires ḥalitza from both of them"? Rather, that sugya is not to be relied upon, as I explained that it does not stand thus; and when [the Gemara] explains that Shmuel is speaking of [a case where] "he began and he did not begin," it will no longer say that Shmuel spoke in accordance with the one who says the levirate bond is not substantial, as I will explain, for according to him [who holds the levirate bond is not substantial], if he performed ḥalitza with sisters or with the recipient of a bill of divorce, the co-wives are exempted. Therefore, we rightly read: "From [the fact] that it says, 'This one performs ḥalitza with one, etc.,' he holds the levirate bond is substantial; and from [the fact] that it says, 'The middle one requires ḥalitza from both of them,' he holds that an invalid ḥalitza must be repeated" — and even though he could infer both from the latter clause, nevertheless, what he can infer from the first clause, he infers [from the first clause].

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:3:2.hebrew: וחליצה פסולה צריך לחזור וכו' - לא כמו שפירש בקונטרס, דכל היכא שאינו יכול לייבם חשיבה חליצה פסולה. דהא אמר בפ"ק (לעיל יבמות דף יא:) גבי מחזיר גרושתו: "או היא או צרתה חולצת", ולא חשיבה חליצת גרושה חליצה פסולה, אע"ג דאין יכול לייבמה. ולקמן נמי קאמר: "אלא צרה דלאה תפטר, דחליצתה כשרה" — אלמא חשיבא לה חליצה כשרה, אע"ג דאסירא ליבמה משום ביטול מצות יבמין. דנהי דלא מבטל מצות יבמין מצרת רחל — דאע"ג דכשייבם לאה יהיה אסור בצרת רחל כמו שאסור בצרת קרובת חלוצתו, מ"מ חליצה מיהא בעיא דאורייתא, דאינה צרת אחות אשה לאחר שיבם לאה, כיון שכבר לא היתה צרת אחות אשה משמת בעלה, וכשיחלוץ לצרת רחל לא מיתסרא לאה, דמותר אדם בקרובת צרת חלוצתו — מ"מ איכא ביטול מצות יבמין אם יבא לייבם לאה, דחיישינן שמא תמות צרת רחל וקא מבטל מרחל מצות יבמין. וליכא למימר דיש לרחל צרות הרבה, דליכא למיחש למיתה דכולהו, אי נמי כשחלץ ללאה קודם נפילת רחל — א"כ, בחנם דחק לתרץ מאי "לא נפטרו צרות" אצרות רחל, ומאי "צרות" — צרות דעלמא; דה"ל לאוקומי טפי בנפול בבת אחת, ואין כי אם צרה אחת ללאה וצרה אחת לרחל, דאז אסורה לייבם לאה משום ביטול מצות יבמין. אלא נראה לר"י, דלא חשיבא חליצה פסולה אלא אחות זקוקתו למ"ד יש זיקה, או אחות חלוצתו לכ"ע, ובעלת הגט ובעלת מאמר, דבכולהו קלשא זיקה: דאחות זקוקתו דמיא לאחות אשתו, דאין בה זיקה; ואחות חלוצתו — כאחות גרושתו; ובעלת הגט דמיא לחלוצה; ובעלת מאמר — לכנוסה, דאין בה זיקה. וכן סוטה דרבנן, דקרי ליה בירושלמי "חליצה פסולה", גבי הא דא"ר שמעון "ביאתה כו'", דדמיא נמי לסוטה דאורייתא, דאין בה זיקה, דטומאה כתיב בה כעריות. אבל מחזיר גרושתו ואסור לבטל מצות יבמין — לא נגרעה בהם הזיקה, ולהכי חשיבי חליצה כשרה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:3:2.english: And invalid ḥalitza must be repeated, etc. - This is not as Rashi explained, that wherever he cannot perform levirate marriage it is considered invalid ḥalitza. For [the Gemara] stated in the first chapter (above, Yevamot 11b) regarding one who remarries his divorcee: "Either she or her co-wife performs ḥalitza," and the ḥalitza of the divorcee is not considered invalid ḥalitza, even though he cannot perform levirate marriage with her. And later too [the Gemara] says: "Rather, let Leah's co-wife be exempt, for her ḥalitza is valid" — thus it is considered valid ḥalitza, even though it is forbidden to perform levirate marriage with her due to nullifying the mitzvah of levirate marriage. For although he does not nullify the mitzvah of levirate marriage with respect to Rachel's co-wife — for even though when he performs levirate marriage with Leah, Rachel's co-wife will be forbidden to him just as the co-wife of a relative of his ḥalutza is forbidden, nevertheless she at least requires ḥalitza by biblical law, since she is not the co-wife of a wife's sister after he has performed levirate marriage with Leah, as she already ceased to be the co-wife of a wife's sister once her husband died, and when he performs ḥalitza with Rachel's co-wife, Leah does not become forbidden, since a man is permitted to [marry] the relative of his ḥalutza's co-wife — nevertheless, there is nullification of the mitzvah of levirate marriage if he comes to perform levirate marriage with Leah, because we are concerned lest Rachel's co-wife die and he will have nullified the mitzvah of levirate marriage from Rachel. And one cannot say that Rachel has many co-wives, such that there is no concern that all of them will die, or alternatively [that it refers to] when he performed ḥalitza with Leah before Rachel fell [for levirate marriage] — for if so, [the Gemara] needlessly forced itself to explain what "co-wives are not exempted" refers to [as] Rachel's co-wives, and why [it says] "co-wives" [in the plural, as] co-wives in general; for it would have been much better to establish it in a case where they fell simultaneously and there is only one co-wife for Leah and one co-wife for Rachel, in which case it is forbidden to perform levirate marriage with Leah due to nullifying the mitzvah of levirate marriage. Rather, it appears to R"I [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that [a case] is not considered invalid ḥalitza except for the sister of his zekukah [woman bound to him by the levirate bond] according to the one who holds that the levirate bond is substantial, or the sister of his ḥalutza according to all opinions, and the recipient of a get [bill of divorce], and the recipient of a ma'amar [levirate betrothal], for in all of these the levirate bond is weakened: the sister of his zekukah resembles his wife's sister, where there is no levirate bond; the sister of his ḥalutza is like his divorcee's sister; the recipient of a get resembles a ḥalutza; and the recipient of a ma'amar [resembles] a married [widow], where there is no levirate bond. And similarly a sotah [suspected adulteress] by rabbinic law, which the Yerushalmi calls "invalid ḥalitza" regarding that which R. Shimon said, "her intercourse, etc.," because she also resembles a sotah by biblical law, where there is no levirate bond, since "defilement" is written regarding her as [it is regarding] forbidden relatives. However, [in the cases of] one who remarries his divorcee and [one who is] forbidden to nullify the mitzvah of levirate marriage, the levirate bond is not diminished in them, and therefore they are considered valid ḥalitza.

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:5:1.hebrew: דנפול בזה אחר זה נפלה חדא חלץ לה ראובן כו' - הקשה ה"ר אברהם מבורגויי"ל: אמאי נקט שלש אחיות? דחידוש זה יכול להשמיענו אפי' בב' אחיות היכא דנפול בבת אחת, דכל אחד ואחד חולץ לשתיהן משום דיש זיקה וחליצה פסולה צריכה לחזור על כל האחין. ותי': דהתם משכחת לה שמתייבמת אחת, דכשחלץ לשניה הויא ראשונה יבמה שהותרה ונאסרה וחזרה והותרה, דתחזור להיתירה הראשון ומתייבמת לאח השני; אע"ג דגם השני צריך לחלוץ לשניה משום דחליצה פסולה היא, מ"מ אינה אסורה לו הראשונה משום אחות חלוצתו, דכיון דחליצה זו לא עשה אלא משום חיזור — כדמוכח לקמן (יבמות דף כז:), דפריך רבי יוסי בר' חנינא לר' יוחנן, דאמר מתה השניה מותר בראשונה, ממתני' דקתני: "חולצות שתיהן ולא מתייבמות", ואמאי? ליקו חד מינייהו ולחלוץ לשניה כו', והשיב לו ר' יוחנן: "אחיות איני יודע מי שנאן" — ואמאי לא שני ליה דחולצות ולא מתייבמות משום דשניה צריכה חליצה משניהם ולכך אסורה לשניהם הראשונה? אלא ודאי לשני שריא, כיון דלא חלץ לה אלא משום חיזור. ואין ראיה, דאיכא למימר דר' יוחנן לא בעי לשנויי הכי משום דסבר כשמואל דחליצה פסולה אין צריך לחזור, ולפי סברתו היה יכול לומר דבשתי אחיות שריא אפי' שניה לשני אם שחלצו לראשונה, דרב לא מפליג לקמן בין ראשונה לשניה, דאמר לקמן: אפי' מתה ראשונה מותר בשניה. ואין נראה לר"י, דלעיל פ"ב (יבמות ד' יח.) משמע דלכ"ע, בין למ"ד יש זיקה בין למ"ד אין זיקה, שתיהן חולצות — אי משום ביטול מצות יבמין או משום שנאסרה עליו שעה אחת, כדפי' לעיל; ודוקא ר' יוחנן הוא דאמר "אחיות איני יודע מי שנאן", ומתייבמת הראשונה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:5:1.english: Where they happened one after the other, [e.g.,] one happened [and] Reuven performed ḥalitza with her, etc. - Rabbi Avraham of Bourgueil raised a difficulty: Why did [the Gemara] mention three sisters? For it could have taught us this novel point even with two sisters, where they happened simultaneously, for each one [of the brothers] performs ḥalitza with both of them, because there is a levirate bond (zikah) and a disqualified ḥalitza must go around to all the brothers! And he answered: There [in the case of two sisters], you find a case where one [of them] can be taken in levirate marriage (yibum), for when [one brother] performs ḥalitza with the second [sister], the first becomes a yevamah who was permitted, then forbidden, and then became permitted again, so that she returns to her original permitted state and may be taken in yibum by the second brother. Even though the second [brother] must also perform ḥalitza with the second [sister] because it is a disqualified ḥalitza, nevertheless the first [sister] is not forbidden to him as the sister of his ḥalutzah, because since he performed this ḥalitza only to fulfill the requirement of going around [to all the brothers] — as is proven below (Yevamot 27b), where Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Ḥanina challenges Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that if the second [sister] died, [the brother] is permitted to the first, from the Mishnah that teaches: "They both perform ḥalitza and may not be taken in yibum," and why? Let one of them arise and perform ḥalitza with the second, etc., and Rabbi Yoḥanan replied to him: "[Regarding] sisters, I do not know who taught it" — now, why did [Rabbi Yoḥanan] not answer him that they perform ḥalitza and may not be taken in yibum because the second [sister] requires ḥalitza from both of them, and therefore the first [sister] is forbidden to both of them? Rather, it must certainly be that [the first sister] is permitted to the second [brother], since he only performed ḥalitza with her [the second sister] to fulfill the requirement of going around. However, there is no proof [from here], for one can say that Rabbi Yoḥanan did not want to answer thus because he holds like Shmuel, that a disqualified ḥalitza does not need to go around [to all the brothers]; and according to his view, he could have said that with two sisters, even the second [sister] is permitted to the second [brother] if they performed ḥalitza with the first, since Rav does not distinguish below between the first and the second, as he says below: Even if the first died, he is permitted to the second. And this does not appear [correct] to Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak], for above in the second chapter (Yevamot 18a) it is implied that according to all opinions — both according to the one who says there is zikah and according to the one who says there is no zikah — both perform ḥalitza, either because of nullifying the mitzvah of yevamim or because she was forbidden to him for one moment, as explained above; and it is only Rabbi Yoḥanan who says, "[Regarding] sisters, I do not know who taught it," and [according to him] the first [sister] may be taken in yibum:

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:6:1.hebrew: נפלה אידך חליץ לה כו' - והא דקרי לה אמצעית, אע"פ שהיא אחרונה — משום דהאחרות כל אחת לא חלצה אלא מן האחד, וזו חולצת משניהם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:6:1.english: "Another [sister] happened [before them], [Shimon] performed ḥalitza with her, etc." - And [as for] that which it calls her "the middle one," even though she is the last [sister] — [this is] because [of] the other [sisters], each one performed ḥalitza with only one [brother], whereas this one performs ḥalitza with both of them:

Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:8:1.hebrew: לדברי האומר יש זיקה קאמר - ולא מסתברא ליה למימר דרב סבר יש זיקה, וההיא דשומרת יבם לדברי האומרים אין זיקה קאמר, משום דהתם קמ"ל תרתי: דאין זיקה, ומחיים אסור משום ביטול מצות יבמין; משום הכי סבירא ליה דההיא אליבא דנפשיה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26b:8:1.english: He is speaking in accordance with the view of the one who says there is zikah - And it does not seem reasonable to [the Gemara] to say that Rav holds there is zikah, and that [statement] regarding a shomeret yavam [a widow awaiting levirate marriage] he stated in accordance with the view of those who say there is no zikah, because there he teaches us two things: that there is no zikah, and that while alive it is forbidden because of nullifying the mitzvah of levirate marriage; therefore, [the Gemara] holds that that [statement] is according to his own view.
